overview: This concurrent resolution, approved by both the House and the Senate, allowed Emancipation Hall in the Capitol Visitor Center to be used on April 29, 2025, for a ceremony presenting the Congressional Gold Medal to the "Six Triple Eight." That unit, the 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion, was made up mostly of Black women who sorted a huge backlog of mail for U.S. troops in Europe during World War II, and Congress awarded it the medal in a 2022 law. The resolution leaves the physical setup of the ceremony to the Architect of the Capitol, the office that runs the Capitol buildings. It does not change any other law or spending. Both chambers had agreed to it as of April 14, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution makes room in the Capitol to properly honor women whose wartime service went unrecognized for decades.
against: Critics say the resolution is a routine, symbolic measure that does not change any law or spending.
